# Atthavasapakaraṇa (Pvr 9)

**ID:** Pvr 9
**Section:** Parivāra (pvr)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Atthavasapakaraṇa
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** The ten reasons for the laying down of training rules
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/pli-tv-pvr9
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m4.mul5.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Atthavasapakaraṇa* ("Exposition of Reasons") is a concise treatise belonging to the *Parivāra*, the final collection of the Vinaya Piṭaka [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI; SuttaCentral]. Its primary subject is an explanation of the ten reasons or purposes (*atthavasa*) for which training rules were laid down by the Buddha for his disciples: the excellence of the Saṅgha, the comfort of the Saṅgha, the restraint of evil-minded individuals, the living in comfort of well-behaved monastics, and the restraint of present and future defilements or cankers (*āsava*) [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI; SuttaCentral]. In modern digital editions it is numbered as Pvr 9, but in the structure analyzed by I. B. Horner, it constitutes the second division of Chapter VII, concluding with the explicit colophon *Atthavasapakaraṇaṃ niṭṭhitaṃ* before the end of the *Parivāra*'s *Mahāvagga* section [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI; Horner, Parivara]. Horner observes that counting this text and its preceding division (*Uposathādivissajjanā*) as separate chapters helps arrive at the traditional count of sixteen *parivāras* recorded in the commentaries [Horner, Parivara].

SuttaCentral notes thematic parallels and mentions of this formula in the Upālisutta (AN 10.31) and the Katthapaññattivāra (Pvr 1.1) [SuttaCentral]. DharmaNexus identifies 141 Pali-internal text-reuse matches across 12 texts, sharing substantial formulaic passages with the *Sāratthadīpanī-ṭīkā*, *Katthapaññattivāra* (Pvr 1.1 and Pvr 2.1), the *Pārājikakaṇḍa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Vajirabuddhi-ṭīkā*, Vinaya rule analyses in the *Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga* (Bu-Vb Pj1) and *Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga* (Bi-Vb Pj5), the *Pañcavagga* (Pvr 21), and the *Aṅguttara Nikāya* (AN 2 and AN 10) [DharmaNexus]. In cross-language alignments, DharmaNexus detects text reuse with the Tibetan translation of the *Yogācārabhūmau Vinayasaṃgrahaṇī* (D4040) and *Vyutpatti* (D4346), as well as Sanskrit fragments of the *Prātimokṣasūtra* [DharmaNexus]. The text was translated into English by I. B. Horner and by Bhikkhu Brahmali [Horner, Book of the Discipline VI; SuttaCentral].
